title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 219 (Power of inspector to conduct investigation into affairs of related companies, etc.)

content.overview: Section 219 provides that if an inspector appointed under section 210 or 212 or 213 or 216 to investigate the affairs of a company considers it necessary for the purposes of investigation to investigate also the affairs of any other body corporate which is or has at any relevant time been the company’s subsidiary or holding company, or a subsidiary of its holding company, or a holding company of its subsidiary, or of any person who is or has been managing director or manager of the company, he may do so with the prior approval of the Central Government. The power prevents a group from parking relevant affairs in a related entity outside the original investigation mandate.
content.glance: Inspector investigating under ss. 210/212/213/216 may, with prior CG approval, also investigate affairs of related body corporates (subsidiary/holding links) or of managing director/manager; prevents group-structure evasion.
content.study: If an inspector appointed under section 210 or section 212 or section 213 or section 216 to investigate the affairs of a company thinks it necessary for the purposes of his investigation to investigate also the affairs of—(a) any other body corporate which is, or has at any relevant time been, the company’s subsidiary or holding company, or a subsidiary of its holding company, or a holding company of its subsidiary; or (b) any person who is or has at any relevant time been the company’s managing director or manager, he shall, with the prior approval of the Central Government, investigate into and report on the affairs of the other body corporate or of the managing director or manager. Current-law framing: confirm original appointment under ss. 210/212/213/216; identify related body corporate or MD/manager within the statutory relationships; obtain prior Central Government approval; then extend the investigation.

sections.heading: Source Appointment
sections.body: Inspector must already be appointed under s. 210, 212, 213 or 216.

sections.heading: Related Targets
sections.body: Other body corporate in subsidiary/holding relationships at the relevant time, or a person who is or has been MD or manager of the company.

sections.heading: Prior Approval
sections.body: Prior approval of the Central Government is required before investigating the related affairs.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Extension only where necessary for the purposes of the original investigation.

provisions.title: Power of inspector to conduct investigation into affairs of related companies, etc.

examples.title: Subsidiary extension
examples.body: An inspector appointed under s. 210 finds that key transactions were routed through a wholly owned subsidiary. With prior CG approval under s. 219, the inspector may investigate the subsidiary’s affairs as well.

examples.title: Approval is mandatory
examples.body: An inspector extends investigation to a holding company without Central Government approval. Section 219 requires prior approval; the extension without it is not authorised.

hypotheticals.question: May an inspector under s. 219 investigate any company in the same industry without approval?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 219 is limited to specified related body corporates (subsidiary/holding links at the relevant time) and to the company’s MD or manager, and requires prior Central Government approval. It is not a free licence to investigate unrelated entities.

distinctions.title: Related-company extension (s. 219) vs original affairs investigation (s. 210)
distinctions.left: Extension of an existing investigation to related bodies/MD/manager with CG approval
distinctions.right: Original CG order to investigate a company’s affairs

misconceptions.trap: Once appointed, an inspector may freely investigate any group company without further approval.
misconceptions.correction: Section 219 requires prior Central Government approval before the inspector investigates specified related body corporates or the MD/manager.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 219 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm source appointment (ss. 210/212/213/216). II. Map related target. III. Require prior CG approval. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Original appointment; related entity facts; approval status; precise relief.

enhancement.definition: Section 219 allows an inspector already appointed under ss. 210, 212, 213 or 216 to investigate, with prior Central Government approval, the affairs of specified related body corporates or of the company’s managing director or manager where necessary for the original investigation.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Group structures cannot be used to place relevant affairs beyond the reach of an investigation already properly ordered.
essentialIngredients: Related body corporate (subsidiary/holding links) or MD/manager
Necessary for purposes of the investigation
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 219 is the related-entity extension power for ongoing statutory investigations.
